slides.title: Bitcoin's hashrate just hit a 7-month high. What is it?
slides.sub: The number behind Bitcoin's security, explained with real data.

slides.title: What hashrate means
paras: Miners race to solve a puzzle to add each new Bitcoin block. Hashrate is <g>how many guesses per second</g> the whole network makes.
Today that's about <g>1,053 EH/s</g> on a 7-day average. One EH/s is a billion billion guesses per second.

slides.title: One year of hashrate
paras: Hashrate dipped through the summer, around the time Bitcoin hit its yearly low (June 30).
<u>It's now back to its highest level since early March.</u>

slides.title: The 2-week reset
paras: Every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks), Bitcoin adjusts its <g>difficulty</g> so blocks keep coming every ~10 minutes, no matter how many miners join.
More hashrate → harder puzzle. The next reset is estimated at <g>+3.3%</g>.
slides.source: mempool.space, Oct 23, 2026 (next change is an estimate)

slides.title: 3 years of growth
paras: In October 2023 the network ran at about 462 EH/s. Today it's <g>about 2.4x</g> that.
<u>A bigger hashrate makes the network more expensive to attack.</u>

slides.title: Does it move price?
paras: Not directly. Read it as a health check, not a trading signal:

items.t: Rising hashrate = miners <g>investing</g> in the network
It usually follows price, with a lag
Falling hashrate can mean miners are <r>under pressure</r>
Difficulty resets keep blocks at ~10 minutes
Check it on free sites like mempool.space
